_comment: Fictional demo data for HarborClaim. Each entry in `scenarios` is seeded into a real running instance by seed_demo_data.py via real HTTP requests -- it is not a fixture loaded directly into the database. `validation_failures` are documented separately because, by design, they can never become a stored claim at all; seed_demo_data.py submits them too, expecting the request to be rejected, and fails loudly if one is ever accepted.

scenarios.label: Straightforward collision, complete on first submission, later approved
scenarios.description: Rear-end collision in a parking lot near the office. Minor bumper and taillight damage.
scenarios.covers: the baseline success path end to end: complete claim -> extraction finds real facts in two documents -> adjuster approves -> claimant is notified

scenarios.label: Theft claim, complete, later declined
scenarios.description: Power tools reported stolen from a locked garage over the weekend.
scenarios.covers: a complete claim that still ends in a non-approval decision -- proves the adjuster decision is a genuine, independent human judgment call, not something the completeness check predetermines

scenarios.label: Vandalism claim, complete, routed for further review
scenarios.description: Storefront window shattered and exterior wall vandalized with graffiti overnight.
scenarios.covers: the third decision outcome (neither approved nor declined) -- an adjuster can route a complete claim back for more review rather than being forced into a binary choice

scenarios.label: Water damage claim, submitted without an incident date
scenarios.description: Pipe failure caused water damage to kitchen flooring and lower cabinets.
scenarios.covers: the completeness checker's NEEDS_INFORMATION path -- same claimant as scenario 1, a second claim, so "My Claims" has more than one entry to show

scenarios.label: Injury claim, no supporting documents attached
scenarios.description: Slip-and-fall on the insured premises, minor wrist sprain, outpatient treatment sought same day.
scenarios.covers: the other way a claim can be incomplete -- all three text fields present and well-formed, zero documents attached. (injury_claim_notes_sample.pdf exists in this folder and matches this scenario's story, but is deliberately NOT attached here -- that's the whole point of this case.)

validation_failures.label: Policy ID over the 40-character limit
validation_failures.description: This submission should never be stored.

validation_failures.label: Incident date in the future
validation_failures.description: An incident that, per the date given, has not happened yet.

validation_failures.label: Uploaded file type not on the allowlist
validation_failures.description: A claim that tries to attach an executable instead of a document.
